_comment: Performance budgets, in gzipped KB as GitHub Pages serves them.
`ceiling` fails the check — it is today's value plus a little headroom, so nothing regresses.
`target` is where docs/INVARIANTS.md says we are going; it is reported, not enforced.
When a phase lands and the real number drops below `target`, LOWER the ceiling to the new
value + headroom in the same commit. That is how the ratchet works — a budget that is never
tightened is a budget that is never met.

boot.why: Everything needed to paint the hero and the first 25 cards. INTENT-2 (speed is the product).

search.why: Everything that must land before a text query can be answered. The single biggest lever on felt speed — see PERF-UX-AUDIT-2026-09-14.md S1 and E1. Phase 4 (I1) is a real, measured regression here, accepted deliberately: content-derived ids (up to ~4.29 billion, vs the old 0..8101 positional ones) serialize as up to 10 digits instead of 1-4, and qtext.json/variants became id-keyed objects instead of position-indexed arrays (required for correctness — see DECISION-11). Measured 1728.2 KB (post-T3) -> 2058.5 KB (post-I1), +330.3 KB / +19.1%. Ceiling carries ~55 KB headroom for corpus growth between sessions, same margin as before. Phase 5's inverted index (a purpose-built compact format, not general-purpose JSON) is what reaches the 800 KB target — id compactness is explicitly deferred there, not chased here (DECISION-9: don't optimize what hasn't been profiled as a real problem).

app_js.why: DECISION-2 (no framework, no bundler). If this creeps past ~28 KB gz, something was added that probably belongs in a lazy-loaded module.
